data.narrative: Completed Module 5 failure mode analysis - chose fail-closed as default stance (never produce incorrect behavior, trade availability for correctness). Created failure mode table with 16 entries covering database, cache, external APIs, infrastructure failures. Identified risk surface: 12 of 16 entries show crash/hang/unhandled. Simulated two failures: database stopped (30s hang then 500), 1ms timeout (unhandled exception). Added DNS resolution failure to table after BREAK exercise. Distinguished transient failures (retry with backoff) from permanent failures (fail fast). Implemented basic handling for DNS failure: meaningful error messages, health checks, cached IPs.

Distinguished transient from permanent failures. Simulated failures to validate assumptions.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Decision summary: 'Chose fail-closed as default stance. Never produce incorrect behavior, trade availability for correctness. Selective fail-open for non-critical features'
Micro-exercise summary: 'Slow is more dangerous than down. Down triggers immediate error handling, slow drains resources until collapse. Every external call needs timeout'
Verification summary: 'Transient failures (network blips, connection timeouts) retry with backoff. Permanent failures (invalid credentials, schema errors) fail fast without retrying'

learning_style_signals: values proactive failure analysis over reactive debugging
prefers fail-closed for correctness with selective fail-open for availability
